title: wringer.diagnosis.v1
description:
A ROUTING DIAGNOSIS, NEVER A VERDICT. Why a loop's final failing gate may have failed, as a guess read out of its output — and nothing that reads this file may let it reach a verdict: not acceptance's receipts, not vacuity, not health. `health.genuine_failure` keeps discounting exit 127 from the exit code it reads itself, never from this. SPEC_ENV_V0 ruling 1 is the boundary and this sentence is it, verbatim.

A SIBLING file in the loop bundle, beside `manifest.json`, on the `usage.json` and `vacuity.json` precedent. It is not a field on the loop manifest's `result` because that object is `additionalProperties: false` in the published and frozen `wringer.loop.v2` manifest schema — SPEC_ENV's ruling 3 asked for exactly that field and could not have it. Law 7: a new file is always allowed, a field on a frozen shape never is.

ABSENT rather than null when the final failure matched no face. A reader that finds this file knows the environment was implicated; a reader that does not find one is not reading a null and wondering.

face.description: Which shape the failure wore. A CLOSED enum, because a face with no name is a face no reader can route on, and `diagnose.FACES` is the single definition it is derived from. `command_not_found`: the shell could not find the command at all (exit 127, or the text). `missing_module`: an interpreter started and could not import something (`No module named`). `not_executable`: the file was found and could not be run (exit 126, or `Permission denied`).

gate.description: The id of the gate this diagnosis is about — the one the verification stopped on.

evidence.description: The line the guess was read from, extracted by `gates.cite` — the single evidence-line extractor in the codebase, which a vacuity row about the same gate would quote identically. The LAST informative line of stderr then stdout, because the first is a traceback header or a row of `=`: true, and no use. Two records citing one gate differently would be worse than either.
